analysis.title: Mirion Technologies - 3Q Results - Ramp Risk Clears, Margin Risk Arrives; Backlog Supports Further Top Line Growth
key_insights: Mirion was on Positive Catalyst Watch into the print on backlog conversion supporting a 2H26 step up in organic growth. FY26 organic revenue growth guidance was raised to 7-8% (from 5-7%), implying high-teens organic growth in 4Q26 versus 1.1% in 2Q26 and 6.5% in 3Q26.

3Q26 adj. EBITDA margin of 23.3% landed below JPM and consensus (24.4%). JPM attributes the miss to Paragon dilution and mix in Nuclear & Safety, one-time costs, and incremental AI investment ($4M YTD). Management removed its 30% margin target for 2028.
3Q26 revenue was $278M versus consensus $276M, made up of ~6.5% organic growth, ~18.6% acquisition contribution and a ~0.6% FX headwind. Adj. EPS of $0.12 was flat YoY and in line with consensus.
Nuclear & Safety revenue grew ~34% to $194M, but segment margin fell ~240bps to 25.7% on Paragon dilution and mix. Medical revenue rose ~6.7% to $84M with margin up ~190bps to 37.8%.
Nuclear Power orders rose 105% ex-M&A. Six new build wins expected in 4Q26 ($80M) are not yet in backlog. Backlog covers ~36% of FY27 revenue, above historical averages.

JPM says the revenue ramp concern has eased. Nuclear & Safety organic growth is implied at ~19% in 4Q, and 4Q revenue is ~83% covered by backlog, the highest since 2022. JPM's ~7.8% FY27 organic growth estimate is 36% covered by current backlog. Investor focus now shifts to margins.

Management removed the 30% margin target for 2028, citing elevated AI spend and slower Paragon margin realization. JPM calls this a prudent reset. One-time items of ~$1-2M across Paragon and Medical weighed on results. Excluding them, Medical would be ~100bps above consensus while Nuclear & Safety remains ~150bps below.
JPM is lowering FY27/FY28 margins, applying ~50% incremental margins and estimating expansion of ~180bps in FY27 and ~170bps in FY28.

AI and cyber spend is accelerating. ~$4M of YTD opex already exceeds the initial full-year budget, and management now expects FY26 costs of $5M or more plus a few million dollars of capex, with further growth in 2027. The spend caused ~70bps of the quarter's margin headwind, alongside ~50bps from M&A and ~50bps from one-time items.

Orders grew 62% YoY ex-M&A to $340M. Total orders rose 85% to $386M including a $46M Paragon contribution, despite the previously disclosed Chinese debooking. Labs and research orders nearly doubled on two Department of Energy awards.

Large opportunity awards totaled $140M in the quarter ($122M net of the debooking), bringing YTD awards to $244M with no pipeline losses this year. Management targets ~$125M of additional 4Q awards, of which more than $80M relates to French newbuilds under the EDF alliance awaiting EU funding approval.
Total backlog reached $1.25bn versus $816M a year ago. Current-year recognition is projected at $292M and 2027 backlog is $443M, together ~$735M to be recognized across 4Q26 and FY27.

FY26 guidance: revenue growth raised to 24-25% (from 22-24%), organic growth to 7-8%, and adj. FCF to $170-185M (from $155-175M). Adj. EBITDA was narrowed to $285-292M (from $285-300M) on margins of 24.7-25.2%.

JPM maintains an Overweight rating and a $22 Dec-27 price target, based on 19.5x FY27E adj. EBITDA. Estimate changes raise revenue and lower the margin path, so revisions are net negative on adj. EBITDA.

market_movers.rationale: JPM keeps its $22 target on 19.5x FY27E EV/EBITDA. Backlog supports top-line growth while margin expansion estimates are lowered on AI spend and slower Paragon margin improvement.

earnings_insights: MIR 3Q26 adj. EPS $0.12 reported, in line with JPMe $0.12 and consensus $0.12, down 5.4% YoY per JPM's variance table (the text calls it flat YoY).
MIR 3Q26 revenue $278M reported vs consensus $276M and JPMe $280M. JPM's variance table shows it 0.8% above consensus and 0.7% below JPMe.
MIR 3Q26 adj. EBITDA $65M reported vs JPMe $68M and consensus $67M. Adj. EBITDA margin 23.3% vs JPMe and consensus 24.4%.
MIR 3Q26 organic growth 6.5% vs JPMe 7.3%. Medical organic growth was 6.8% vs JPMe 9.3%. Nuclear & Safety organic growth was 6.3% vs JPMe 6.2%.
MIR FY26 guidance after the print: adj. EPS $0.50-0.54 (from $0.48-0.55), adj. EBITDA $285-292M (from $285-300M), adj. FCF $170-185M, revenue growth 24-25%, organic growth 7-8%.
JPM estimates (not reported): 4Q26E revenue $351M, adj. EBITDA $104M, adj. EPS $0.22. FY26E adj. EPS $0.55, FY27E $0.66, FY28E $0.78.
MIR 3Q26 orders of $340M ex-M&A (+62% YoY) and $386M total (+85%) are reported figures. Backlog was $1.25bn.
risk_factors: Nuclear project timing: large reactor-related orders are lumpy, and delays in government approvals or life extension schedules can cause quarterly volatility.
Regulatory dependencies: changes in radiation exposure standards or approval processes could hurt demand.
Execution on integration of Certrec and Paragon: delays could limit synergy capture.
Geopolitical and policy risk: energy policy, tariffs or defense budget reallocations (NATO, DOE programs) may affect order timing and funding.
Competition from Thermo Fisher, AMETEK and Fortive could pressure pricing or accelerate digital investment.
Supply chain and talent: securing germanium and specialized talent remains critical.
Financial leverage: Paragon lifts pro forma leverage to ~3.3x, and higher interest rates or delayed deleveraging could constrain flexibility and lower 2026 EPS estimates.
vol_and_positioning: MIR 90-day volatility is 54 per JPM's company data table.
MIR shares are down 28.5% YTD (-42.5% relative) and 33.5% over 12 months, but up 16.7% over 1 month. The stock trades at $16.75 in a 52-week range of $14.04-$30.28.
Of the 11 analysts in the Bloomberg survey, 10 rate MIR Buy, 1 Hold and 0 Sell. Free float is 96.3% and 3M ADV is $62.6M.
geopolitical: The report names a Chinese debooking that reduced 3Q26 orders.
The report names EU funding approval pending for French newbuilds under the EDF alliance, which is the basis for more than $80M of targeted 4Q awards.
The report lists energy policy shifts, trade tariffs and defense budget reallocations (NATO, DOE programs) as risks to order timing and funding.

tension_points.bull_case: JPM says backlog coverage of 4Q26 (~83%) and FY27 (~36%) supports revenue growth, and it still sees ~170-180bps of annual margin expansion in FY27 and FY28 with high-teens 4Q organic growth. It views the removal of the 30% margin target as a prudent reset.
tension_points.bear_case: 3Q margin missed JPM and consensus on Paragon dilution, one-time costs and AI spend. Management withdrew the 2028 30% margin target, and JPM's revisions are net negative on adj. EBITDA. Nuclear & Safety margin is ~150bps below consensus even excluding one-time items.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Continued margin shortfalls versus consensus in coming quarters, or Paragon margin realization slower than JPM's ~50% incremental margin assumption.

theme_stances.key_argument: Revenue visibility has improved with backlog covering 4Q26 revenue by ~83% and FY27 revenue by ~36%.
theme_stances.evidence: backlog covering ~36% of FY27 revenue, above historical averages

theme_stances.key_argument: Margins came in light, management removed the 2028 margin target, and JPM lowered FY27/FY28 margin expansion.
theme_stances.evidence: Adj. EBITDA margins, however, landed below both our forecast and consensus
